{{Short description|Professor of computer science}}
'''Eran Tromer''' ({{Langx|he|ערן טרומר}}) is a professor of [[computer science]] at [[Boston University]]. His research focuses on [[information security]], [[cryptography]] and [[Algorithm|algorithms]].<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |title=Eran Tromer |website=[[Boston University College of Arts and Sciences]] |url=https://www.bu.edu/cs/profiles/eran-tromer/}}</ref><ref name="welcomes">{{Cite web |title=Hariri Institute Welcomes New Faculty Affiliates Eran Tromer (CS) and Tianyu Wang (ENG) |last=Wojtanik |first=Chloe |url=https://www.bu.edu/hic/2024/04/05/hariri-institute-welcomes-new-faculty-affiliates-tromer-wang/}}</ref> He is a founding scientist of [[Zcash]].<ref name="bio" /><ref name="spectrum">{{Cite magazine |title=The Crazy Security Behind the Birth of Zcash, the Inside Story |last=Peck |first=Morgen |magazine=[[IEEE Spectrum]] |url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/the-crazy-security-behind-the-birth-of-zcash}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Tromer received his PhD from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref name="bio" /> In 2024, he joined Boston University's Hariri Institute for Computing.<ref name="welcomes" />

== Research ==
In 2014, Tromer and his colleagues demonstrated an RSA key extraction attack using [[acoustic cryptanalysis]], a type of side-channel attack.<ref>{{Cite conference |title=RSA Key Extraction via Low-Bandwidth Acoustic Cryptanalysis |last1=Genkin |first1=Daniel |last2=Shamir |first2=Adi |author-link2=Adi Shamir |last3=Tromer |first3=Eran |conference=Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO 2014}}</ref><ref name="spectrum" />

In 2014, Tromer coauthored the design of Zerocash,<ref>{{Cite conference |title=Zerocash: Decentralized Anonymous Payments from Bitcoin |last1=Ben-Sasson | first1=Eli |author-link1=Eli Ben-Sasson |last2=Chiesa |first2=Alessandro |author-link2=Alessandro Chiesa |last3=Garman |first3=Christina |last4=Green |first4=Matthew |author-link4=Matthew D. Green |last5=Miers |first5=Ian |last6=Eran |first6=Tromer |last7=Virza |first7=Madars |conference=2014 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy}}</ref> which laid the foundation for the [[Zcash]] protocol. The work was recognized by the Test of Time Award at the [[IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy]].<ref name="test of time">{{Cite web |title=45th IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy |url=https://sp2024.ieee-security.org/awards.html}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* [[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]] CCS The Test-of-Time Award (2019)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sigsac.org/ccs/CCS_awards/ccs-tta.html | title=ACM CCS the Test-of-Time Awards }}</ref>
* [[IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy]] Test-of-Time Award (2024)<ref name="test of time" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eran Tromer Honored with the Test of Time Award at the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P) 2024 |url=https://www.bu.edu/hic/2024/06/27/eran-tromer-honored-with-the-test-of-time-award-at-the-ieee-symposium-on-security-and-privacy-sp-2024/}}</ref>
